question: Choose the sentence with no spelling error.
option_1: Near death expereinces are stil near death.
option_2: Near death expriences are still near death.
option_3: Near death experiences are stil near deaath.
option_4: Near death experiences are still near death.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Near death experiences are still near death.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Only Option 4 spells every word correctly: experiences (अनुभव), still (अब भी) and death (मृत्यु).

◦ “Experience” = ex + peri + ence; the vowel order is e-r-i-e, so “expereince/exprience” are misspellings.

◦ “Still” always has a double l; “stil” is wrong.

◦ Correct: Near death experiences are still near death.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 has two errors — “expereinces” and “stil”.

• Option 2 misspells “experiences” as “expriences” (the letter ‘e’ after ‘p’ is dropped).

• Option 3 has “stil” and “deaath”, both misspelt.

NOTE

• Commonly misspelt SSC words: experience, existence, occurrence, embarrass, maintenance, privilege, separate.

• Spelling trick: words ending in -ence (existence, occurrence) vs -ance (maintenance, appearance) are a favourite MTS/CHSL trap.

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

Producing a different component was as simple such launching a new computer program.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. as simple such launching.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is a comparison of equality, and the fixed structure for that is as + adjective + as, never “as … such”. (समान तुलना)

◦ So “as simple such launching” must become “as simple as launching”.

◦ The word after the second “as” is a gerund (“launching”), which correctly parallels the gerund “Producing” at the start.

◦ Correct: Producing a different component was as simple as launching a new computer program.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 ‘No error’ is wrong because the sentence clearly contains a comparison error.

• Option 2 “Producing a different component was” is correct — a gerund phrase as subject takes a singular verb.

• Option 4 “a new computer program.” is a correct object phrase.

NOTE

• Comparison patterns: as … as (equality), not so/as … as (negative), -er than / more … than (comparative), the … est / most (superlative).

• “Such as” is used only for examples (fruits such as mango), not for comparison of degree.

question:
Select the appropriate antonym for the underlined word.

The beauty of our landscape is important.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. blemish.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Beauty means loveliness, an attractive quality. (सुंदरता)

◦ Blemish means a flaw, spot or defect that spoils appearance. (दाग, दोष) — the exact opposite of beauty.

◦ Correct: The beauty of our landscape is important. — antonym = blemish.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Glamour (आकर्षण) — charm and attractiveness; a synonym, not an antonym.

• Aesthetics (सौंदर्यशास्त्र) — the study or appreciation of beauty; related, not opposite.

• Nobility (कुलीनता) — high moral quality or aristocratic rank; unrelated to beauty.

NOTE

• Synonyms of beauty: elegance, grace, splendour, allure, charm.

• Synonyms of blemish: flaw, stain, defect, taint, imperfection.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the bracketed segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘no substitution required’.

This commodity in clay-coloured material (can’t be used neither as a table mat nor as a table napkin).
option_1: can’t be used either as a table mat or as a table napkin
option_3: can’t be used neither as a table mat but as a table napkin
option_4: can’t be used neither as a table mat or as a table napkin
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. can’t be used either as a table mat or as a table napkin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• English does not allow a double negative. The sentence already has the negative “can’t”, so “neither … nor” (also negative) cannot follow. (दोहरा नकारात्मक)

◦ With an existing negative verb, the correct correlative pair is either … or.

◦ Correlatives must be parallel: either as a table mat or as a table napkin.

◦ Correct: This commodity in clay-coloured material can’t be used either as a table mat or as a table napkin.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 keeps “can’t … neither … nor”, a double negative, so substitution is required.

• Option 3 wrongly mixes “neither … but”, which is not a correlative pair at all.

• Option 4 wrongly mixes “neither … or”; “neither” must be paired with “nor”.

NOTE

• Correlative pairs: either–or, neither–nor, both–and, not only–but also, whether–or.

• “Neither … nor” is itself negative: “He neither ate nor drank” (never “didn’t neither”).

question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

People need to made changes in agriculture and land use.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. made changes in.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Need to” is followed by the to-infinitive, i.e. the bare V1 form of the verb, never the past form V2. (मूल क्रिया रूप)

◦ Hence “to made” is wrong; it must be “to make”.

◦ Correct: People need to make changes in agriculture and land use.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “People need to” is correct — “people” is a plural noun taking the plural verb “need”.

• Option 2 “agriculture and land use.” is a correct object of the preposition “in”.

• Option 3 ‘No error’ is wrong because the verb form after “to” is faulty.

NOTE

• After to (infinitive marker), have to, used to, ought to, able to, going to → always V1.

• Do not confuse with used to / accustomed to / look forward to, where “to” is a preposition and takes V1+ing.

question:
Choose the word that means the same as the given word.

Easiness
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Gullibility.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Easiness here carries the sense of being “easy” to fool — a lack of resistance or over-readiness to believe. (सरलता, भोलापन)

◦ Gullibility means the quality of being easily deceived or cheated. (आसानी से बहकावे में आना)

◦ A person of great easiness of mind is an “easy mark”, i.e. gullible.

◦ Correct: His easiness – that is, his gullibility – made him an easy target for con men.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Immunity (प्रतिरक्षा) — resistance to disease or exemption from an obligation.

• Fraternity (भाईचारा) — brotherhood, a group with common interests.

• Indomitability (अजेयता) — the quality of being unconquerable; the opposite in spirit.

NOTE

• Synonyms of gullible: credulous, naive, unsuspecting, trusting; antonyms: shrewd, sceptical, astute.

• Related SSC vocabulary: dupe (ठगना), credulity (सहज विश्वास), guile (छल).

question: Choose the incorrectly spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Condision.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is Condition (स्थिति, दशा), with the ending -tion, not “-sion”.

◦ Nouns formed from verbs ending in -d/-de usually take -sion (decide → decision), but “condition” comes from Latin *conditio* and takes -tion.

◦ Correct: The patient’s condition improved overnight.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Busy (व्यस्त) is correctly spelt — note the unusual ‘u’ pronounced /ɪ/.

• Plane (विमान / समतल) is correctly spelt; its homophone is “plain” (सादा).

• Sponge (स्पंज) is correctly spelt — ‘g’ is soft before ‘e’.

NOTE

• ‑tion words: condition, position, addition, ambition, competition.

• ‑sion words: decision, division, occasion, permission, admission.

question:
Select the most appropriate word for the given group of words.

Government by two rulers or authorities
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Diarchy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Diarchy (also spelt dyarchy) = rule by two persons or authorities jointly. (द्वैध शासन)

◦ The prefix di-/dy- means “two” and -archy means “rule”.

◦ In Indian history, the Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms) introduced diarchy in the provinces.

◦ Correct: Government by two rulers or authorities is called a diarchy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Monarchy (राजतंत्र) — rule by a single king or queen.

• Bureaucracy (नौकरशाही) — government by appointed officials/departments.

• Anarchy (अराजकता) — absence of government; lawlessness.

NOTE

• One-word substitutes for rule: Autocracy (one person, absolute), Oligarchy (a few), Plutocracy (the wealthy), Theocracy (priests/religion), Democracy (the people), Matriarchy/Patriarchy (mother/father-headed).

question:
Choose the word that can substitute the given group of words.

A case in which the blade of a sword is kept
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Sheath.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A sheath is the close-fitting cover or case for the blade of a sword, knife or dagger. (म्यान)

◦ Related verb: to unsheathe a sword = to draw it out of its sheath.

◦ Correct: He returned the sword to its sheath.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Pantry (भंडार-कक्ष) — a small room where food and crockery are stored.

• Dyke/Dike (बाँध) — an embankment built to hold back water.

• Infirmary (चिकित्सालय) — a place in a school or institution for the sick.

NOTE

• Similar container one-word substitutes: Quiver (case for arrows), Scabbard (sword-case, synonym of sheath), Holster (case for a pistol), Granary (store for grain), Aviary (enclosure for birds), Apiary (place for bees).

question:
Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select ‘No error’.

In another words, most of us / are made by our elders or by our / peers, but leaders are self-directed.
option_2: In another words, most of us
option_3: are made by our elders or by our
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. In another words, most of us.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Another” is always followed by a singular countable noun, whereas “words” is plural. (एकवचन के साथ another)

◦ The fixed idiomatic phrase is “in other words” (दूसरे शब्दों में), used to restate something.

◦ Use other before plural nouns: other words, other people, other books.

◦ Correct: In other words, most of us are made by our elders or by our peers, but leaders are self-directed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “peers, but leaders are self-directed.” is grammatically correct.

• Option 3 “are made by our elders or by our” is a correct passive structure.

• Option 4 ‘No error’ is wrong because the phrase “in another words” is faulty.

NOTE

• Another = an + other → singular (another book); Other → plural (other books); The other → the remaining one of two.

• Useful linkers: in other words, that is to say, namely, to put it differently.

question:
Improve the underlined part of the sentence. Choose ‘No improvement’ as an answer if the sentence is grammatically correct.

At age 25, she taken her vows and became a nun.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. took her vows.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Taken” is the third form (V3/past participle) and cannot be used alone as the main verb — it needs a helping verb (has/have/had/was).

◦ The sentence has no auxiliary, so the simple past (V2) “took” is required.

◦ Parallelism confirms it: the second verb “became” is simple past, so the first must also be simple past.

◦ Correct: At age 25, she took her vows and became a nun. (व्रत लेना)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “take her vows” is present tense and clashes with “became”.

• Option 2 ‘No improvement’ is wrong because “taken” alone is ungrammatical.

• Option 4 “take her vowed” is meaningless — two verbs cannot be joined that way.

NOTE

• Verb forms: take – took – taken; go – went – gone; write – wrote – written.

• V3 is used only with have/has/had (perfect) or be (passive): “She has taken her vows.”

question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option ‘no correction required’ if the sentence is correct as given.

They said that they (were understandings) his theory very well.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. understood.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The reporting verb “said” is in the past tense, so in indirect speech the reported verb also moves to the past tense. (कालों का अनुक्रम / sequence of tenses)

◦ “Understand” is a stative verb (verb of mental state) and is not normally used in the continuous form.

◦ Hence “were understandings” must become the simple past “understood”.

◦ Correct: They said that they understood his theory very well.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “understanding” alone leaves the clause without a finite verb.

• Option 2 ‘No correction required’ is wrong — “were understandings” is doubly faulty (continuous + plural noun form).

• Option 3 “have understand” is wrong; after “have” the V3 “understood” is needed, and the present perfect clashes with “said”.

NOTE

• Stative verbs not used in continuous: know, believe, understand, love, hate, own, seem, want, prefer.

• Reported speech shift: present → past, past → past perfect, will → would, can → could.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To sing a different tune
option_1: To change the way one talks about something
option_3: To be able to handle a jolt
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To change the way one talks about something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom “to sing a different tune” means to change one’s opinion, attitude or the way one speaks about something, usually reversing an earlier stand. (अपना रुख बदल लेना)

◦ It is often used when circumstances force the change: “He criticised the plan, but once he got the contract he sang a different tune.”

◦ A common variant is “to change one’s tune”.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• “To brag about something” = to blow one’s own trumpet, a different idiom.

• “To be able to handle a jolt” = to take something in one’s stride.

• “To buy or sell something” has no idiomatic link with singing a tune.

NOTE

• Related idioms: to call the tune (to be in control), to face the music (to accept unpleasant consequences), to change horses in midstream (to change plans midway).

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

He was ______ in a pool of blood near a neighbour’s house.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. lying.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure “He was ______” needs the present participle (V1+ing) to form the past continuous tense.

◦ The intransitive verb lie (to rest/recline – लेटना) has forms lie – lay – lain – lying; no object follows it.

◦ Since the man is not placing anything, “lay” (to put down – रखना: lay – laid – laid – laying) cannot be used.

◦ Correct: He was lying in a pool of blood near a neighbour’s house.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “lain” is the V3 of “lie” and needs “had/has”, not “was”.

• Option 2 “laying” belongs to the transitive verb “lay”, which requires an object.

• Option 4 “lied” is the past of “lie = to tell an untruth” (झूठ बोलना), wrong in meaning here.

NOTE

• Three ‘lie/lay’ verbs: lie–lay–lain–lying (recline), lay–laid–laid–laying (place), lie–lied–lied–lying (tell a lie).

question:
A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.

You have the power ______ the perspective of this nation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. to change.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The noun power is regularly followed by a to-infinitive when it means the ability or authority to do something. (… करने की शक्ति)

◦ The infinitive here works as an adjective phrase qualifying “power”: power to change, power to decide, power to act.

◦ Correct: You have the power to change the perspective of this nation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “changing” would need a preposition (“power of changing”), which is not the natural idiom.

• Option 3 “change” is a bare verb and leaves two finite verbs (“have” and “change”) with no link.

• Option 4 “changed” is the past form and cannot follow the noun “power”.

NOTE

• Nouns commonly followed by to + V1: ability, chance, opportunity, permission, right, decision, wish, attempt, effort.

• Compare: “He has the ability to solve it” but “He is capable of solving it” (preposition + gerund).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Strength training is useful as it avoids large increases in breathing rate and ______ muscle strength.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. improves.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes why strength training is useful, so the blank must carry a positive sense.

◦ Improves means makes better or enhances (सुधारता है) — exactly what training does to muscle strength.

◦ Correct: Strength training is useful as it avoids large increases in breathing rate and improves muscle strength.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Regresses (पीछे लौटना) — returns to a worse or earlier state; contradicts “useful”.

• Distributes (वितरित करना) — to share out; strength is not distributed.

• Degrades (गिराना, घटाना) — lowers quality; the opposite of the required meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of improve: enhance, augment, ameliorate, boost, refine.

• Antonyms: deteriorate, worsen, impair, degrade, diminish.

question:
Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.

A sudden gust of wind hits the window.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. blow.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A gust is a sudden strong rush of wind. (झोंका)

◦ As a noun, blow likewise means a sudden strong movement of air — “a blow of wind”.

◦ Correct: A sudden gust (= blow) of wind hits the window.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Cramp (ऐंठन) — a painful involuntary contraction of a muscle.

• Feel (महसूस करना) — to sense by touch or emotion; not a wind word.

• Pump (पंप करना) — a device or the act of forcing liquid/air; unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of gust: blast, rush, squall, flurry, puff.

• Wind vocabulary for SSC: breeze (light wind), gale (very strong wind), zephyr (a soft gentle breeze), cyclone/typhoon (violent storm).

question:
In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the Idiom/Phrase.

With a pinch of salt
option_4: Doubt the truth or value of something
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Doubt the truth or value of something.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom “to take something with a pinch of salt” means to accept a statement with reservation, i.e. not to believe it completely. (पूरी तरह विश्वास न करना)

◦ It suggests scepticism about the truth or importance of what is said.

◦ Example: Take his account of the accident with a pinch of salt — he exaggerates.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• “With due respect” is a polite formula used before disagreeing, not this idiom.

• Nefariously (दुष्टतापूर्वक) means wickedly — unrelated.

• “Taken forcefully” is a literal phrase with no idiomatic connection.

NOTE

• The American variant is “with a grain of salt”.

• Related idioms: to take at face value (to believe fully — the opposite), to smell a rat (to suspect something wrong), to cast doubt on (to make people question).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

He gave the horse enough room to ______ away from the wagon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. walk.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the infinitive marker “to”, so it needs a bare V1 that suits “room … away from the wagon”.

◦ Walk away from is the natural collocation for an animal moving off on foot. (दूर चलकर जाना)

◦ Correct: He gave the horse enough room to walk away from the wagon.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 “woke” is the past form (V2) of “wake” and cannot follow “to”; it is also illogical here.

• Option 2 “stalk” means to pursue stealthily — a horse given room does not stalk away.

• Option 4 “watch” means to observe and does not fit “away from the wagon”.

NOTE

• Phrasal usage: walk away from (to leave/abandon), walk out on (to desert), walk over (to defeat easily).

• After to as an infinitive marker, always use V1: to go, to walk, to eat.

question:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Lethargy
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Attention.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Lethargy means a lack of energy, sluggishness and drowsy inattentiveness. (सुस्ती, आलस्य)

◦ Attention implies alertness and active mental engagement (ध्यान, सजगता), which is the opposite state of a lethargic mind.

◦ Among the four choices only “attention” denotes alertness, so it is the best available antonym.

◦ Correct: After a cup of coffee his lethargy gave way to keen attention.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Refusal (इनकार) — the act of saying no; the antonym of acceptance.

• Shield (ढाल) — protection or a protective plate; unrelated to energy.

• Existence (अस्तित्व) — the state of being; unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of lethargy: inertia, torpor, sluggishness, apathy, languor.

• Stronger antonyms often asked: vigour, energy, alertness, vitality, animation.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

By contrast, depression is a (1) ______, long-term downturn in economic activity in one or more (2) ______. A depression is a more (3) ______ downturn than a recession, which is seen by some economists as part of the modern business cycle. The latter refers to (4) ______ that occur around a long-term growth trend, and typically involve shifts over time between (5) ______ of relatively rapid economic growth (an expansion or boom), and periods of relative stagnation or decline (a contraction or recession).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. sustained.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank is an adjective describing the noun phrase “long-term downturn”, so it must convey continued over time.

◦ Sustained means continuing for an extended period without weakening. (लगातार, निरंतर)

◦ It pairs naturally with “long-term”: a sustained, long-term downturn.

◦ Correct: By contrast, depression is a sustained, long-term downturn in economic activity.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Curtained — covered with a curtain; makes no sense with a downturn.

• Abstained — refrained from doing something (e.g. voting); it is intransitive and cannot describe a downturn.

• Stained — marked or discoloured; unrelated to economic duration.

NOTE

• Synonyms of sustained: prolonged, continuous, steady, unremitting, persistent.

• Economics vocabulary: recession (a short-term decline), depression (a deep, prolonged recession), stagnation (no growth).

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

By contrast, depression is a (1) ______, long-term downturn in economic activity in one or more (2) ______. A depression is a more (3) ______ downturn than a recession, which is seen by some economists as part of the modern business cycle. The latter refers to (4) ______ that occur around a long-term growth trend, and typically involve shifts over time between (5) ______ of relatively rapid economic growth (an expansion or boom), and periods of relative stagnation or decline (a contraction or recession).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. economies.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase is “a downturn in economic activity in one or more ______”, so the blank needs a plural noun meaning national economic systems.

◦ Economies = the wealth and resource systems of countries or regions. (अर्थव्यवस्थाएँ)

◦ A depression is described as spreading across one or more national economies.

◦ Correct: … a sustained, long-term downturn in economic activity in one or more economies.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Services — one sector of an economy; too narrow, as the downturn covers all activity.

• Autonomies — states of self-government; not units in which economic activity is measured.

• Astronomies — relating to the study of stars; completely irrelevant.

NOTE

• Do not confuse economy (the system / thrift), economic (relating to the economy) and economical (money-saving, cheap).

• Example: an economical car saves fuel; the economic policy shapes the economy.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

By contrast, depression is a (1) ______, long-term downturn in economic activity in one or more (2) ______. A depression is a more (3) ______ downturn than a recession, which is seen by some economists as part of the modern business cycle. The latter refers to (4) ______ that occur around a long-term growth trend, and typically involve shifts over time between (5) ______ of relatively rapid economic growth (an expansion or boom), and periods of relative stagnation or decline (a contraction or recession).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. severe.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure is a comparison: “a more ______ downturn than a recession”, so the blank needs an adjective used with “more … than”.

◦ Severe means intense, harsh or serious. (गंभीर, कठोर)

◦ A depression is by definition deeper and harsher than a recession, so “more severe” is logical.

◦ Correct: A depression is a more severe downturn than a recession.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Tamed — domesticated or brought under control; contradicts the idea of a worse downturn.

• Feral — wild, having reverted from domestication; used of animals, not economies.

• Simple — easy or uncomplicated; does not fit a comparison of intensity.

NOTE

• Synonyms of severe: acute, grave, harsh, stringent, intense; antonyms: mild, lenient, gentle.

• Adjectives of two or more syllables take more … than (more severe), not ‘-er’.

Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

By contrast, depression is a (1) ______, long-term downturn in economic activity in one or more (2) ______. A depression is a more (3) ______ downturn than a recession, which is seen by some economists as part of the modern business cycle. The latter refers to (4) ______ that occur around a long-term growth trend, and typically involve shifts over time between (5) ______ of relatively rapid economic growth (an expansion or boom), and periods of relative stagnation or decline (a contraction or recession).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. fluctuations.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The clause says these things “occur around a long-term growth trend” and “involve shifts over time” — so the blank needs a plural noun meaning ups and downs.

◦ Fluctuations are irregular rises and falls in level or amount. (उतार-चढ़ाव)

◦ The business cycle is precisely a series of fluctuations around the trend line.

◦ Correct: The latter refers to fluctuations that occur around a long-term growth trend.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Firmness — steadiness or resolve; the opposite of movement around a trend.

• Stability — absence of change; contradicts “shifts over time”.

• Sustainability — the ability to be maintained; also an uncountable idea that does not “occur” around a trend.

NOTE

• Synonyms of fluctuation: variation, oscillation, swing, instability, vacillation.

• Business-cycle phases: expansion (boom) → peak → contraction (recession) → trough → recovery.

question:
Comprehension:

In the following passage some words have been deleted. Fill in the blanks with the help of the alternatives given. Select the most appropriate option for each number.

By contrast, depression is a (1) ______, long-term downturn in economic activity in one or more (2) ______. A depression is a more (3) ______ downturn than a recession, which is seen by some economists as part of the modern business cycle. The latter refers to (4) ______ that occur around a long-term growth trend, and typically involve shifts over time between (5) ______ of relatively rapid economic growth (an expansion or boom), and periods of relative stagnation or decline (a contraction or recession).

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. periods.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is balanced: “shifts … between ______ of relatively rapid economic growth … and periods of relative stagnation or decline”.

◦ Parallel structure demands the same noun in both halves, so the blank must be periods (अवधि, कालखंड).

◦ The preposition “between” also requires a plural noun, which “periods” supplies.

◦ Correct: … shifts over time between periods of relatively rapid economic growth … and periods of relative stagnation or decline.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Perpetually is an adverb (“constantly”) and cannot follow the preposition “between”.

• Perpetuity means an endless duration; it is singular and does not fit “between … and periods”.

• Prods means pokes or urges; meaningless in an economic time context.

NOTE

• Between is used for two items/groups; among for more than two.

• Parallelism rule: items joined by and/or/but must be of the same grammatical form (noun–noun, verb–verb, phrase–phrase).

question: The feature of single citizenship in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from the Constitution of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Britain.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India follows the system of single citizenship, borrowed from the British Constitution — every Indian is a citizen of India only, and not separately of the State in which he/she resides. (एकल नागरिकता)

• Other features borrowed from Britain: Parliamentary form of government, Rule of Law, Legislative procedure, Single citizenship, Cabinet system, Prerogative writs, Bicameralism.

• Citizenship is dealt with in Part II, Articles 5 to 11 of the Constitution; Parliament enacted the Citizenship Act, 1955 under Article 11.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Canada — Federation with a strong Centre, vesting of residuary powers in the Centre, appointment of State Governors by the Centre, advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.

• USA — Fundamental Rights, independence of judiciary, judicial review, impeachment of the President, removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges, post of Vice-President.

• Australia — Concurrent List, freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse, joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament.

NOTE

• Ireland — Directive Principles of State Policy, nomination of members to Rajya Sabha, method of election of the President.

• USSR (erstwhile) — Fundamental Duties and the ideal of justice in the Preamble; South Africa — procedure for amendment of the Constitution and election of Rajya Sabha members.

question: Which among the following is Phanerogams, flowering and seed-bearing plants?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gymnosperms.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Phanerogams (also called Spermatophyta) are plants that bear seeds and have well-differentiated reproductive tissues. (बीजधारी पौधे)

• Phanerogams are divided into Gymnosperms (naked seeds, not enclosed in fruit — pine, deodar, cycas) and Angiosperms (seeds enclosed inside fruits).

• Among the given options, only Gymnosperms belong to Phanerogams; the rest are Cryptogams (non-seed-bearing plants).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Thallophyta — the simplest plants with an undifferentiated thallus body; commonly called algae (Spirogyra, Ulothrix, Chara).

• Bryophyta — the "amphibians of the plant kingdom"; no true vascular tissue (Moss/Funaria, Marchantia, Riccia).

• Pteridophyta — the first plants with true vascular tissue (xylem and phloem) but no seeds (Fern, Marsilea, Equisetum).

NOTE

• Plant kingdom classification by Eichler: Cryptogamae (Thallophyta, Bryophyta, Pteridophyta) and Phanerogamae (Gymnosperms, Angiosperms).

• Angiosperms are further divided into monocotyledons (one seed leaf — maize, wheat) and dicotyledons (two seed leaves — gram, pea).

question: Cosmic snowballs of frozen gases, rock and dust that orbit the Sun are known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Comets.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Comets are icy bodies — "cosmic snowballs" of frozen gases, rock and dust — that revolve around the Sun in highly elongated elliptical orbits. (धूमकेतु)

• On approaching the Sun a comet heats up and forms a glowing coma and a long tail that always points away from the Sun due to solar wind and radiation pressure.

• The most famous is Halley's Comet, which is visible from Earth roughly every 76 years (last seen in 1986, next expected in 2061).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Meteors — commonly called "shooting stars"; small rock/debris fragments that burn up on entering the Earth's atmosphere due to friction.

• Meteorites — meteoroids that survive the fiery passage and actually strike the Earth's surface.

• Stars — huge self-luminous celestial bodies of hot gases (mainly hydrogen and helium) that produce energy by nuclear fusion; the Sun is the nearest star.

NOTE

• Asteroids are rocky bodies mostly found in the asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter; Ceres is the largest.

• The Oort Cloud and the Kuiper Belt are the source regions of long-period and short-period comets respectively.

question: By October 2022, Prime Minister Narendra Modi has inaugurated ______ Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samruddhi Kendras.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 600.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• On 17 October 2022, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated 600 Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samruddhi Kendras (PMKSK) across the country at the PM Kisan Samman Sammelan 2022 held in New Delhi. (प्रधानमंत्री किसान समृद्धि केंद्र)

• PMKSKs are one-stop shops for farmers, providing fertilisers, seeds, agricultural implements, soil-testing facilities and advisory services.

• The scheme comes under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers (Department of Fertilizers); over 3.3 lakh retail fertiliser shops are to be converted into PMKSKs in a phased manner.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• At the same event the PM launched "Bharat" — One Nation One Fertilizer (single brand name for all subsidised fertilisers) and the Indian Edge e-magazine on agriculture.

• He also released the 12th instalment of PM-KISAN funds (about Rs. 16,000 crore) to crores of beneficiary farmers.

NOTE

• PM-KISAN (launched 24 February 2019) gives Rs. 6,000 per year in three equal instalments of Rs. 2,000 to landholding farmer families.

• Other farmer-centric schemes: PMFBY (crop insurance, 2016), Soil Health Card (2015), e-NAM (2016), PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (2015).

question: Which among the following is a ritual of cleaning the earth as well as worshipping the fourteen gods in Tripura, India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kharchi Puja.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kharchi Puja is a famous week-long festival of Tripura, celebrated at the Chaturdasha Devata Temple at Old Agartala (Khayerpur) in the month of July (Ashadha). (खारची पूजा)

• The word "Kharchi" derives from "khya" (earth) — the festival is essentially a ritual of cleansing/purifying the earth of the sins of its people, along with the worship of the fourteen gods (Chaturdasha Devata) of the royal Tripuri family.

• Originally a tribal festival of the Tripuri people, it is today celebrated by both tribal and non-tribal communities of the State.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Tusu — a harvest festival of the Jharkhand–West Bengal (Purulia)–Odisha belt, celebrated in the month of Poush by unmarried girls in honour of the maiden goddess Tusu.

• Durga Puja — the great autumn festival of West Bengal, inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2021.

• Bani — a ritual festival associated with Andhra Pradesh (Devaragattu, Kurnool district), known for its stick-fight ritual.

NOTE

• Other festivals of Tripura: Garia Puja, Ker Puja, Ashokastami, Orange and Tourism Festival.

• Tripura's major tribes: Tripuri, Reang (Bru), Jamatia, Chakma, Halam, Noatia, Mog; the Ujjayanta Palace in Agartala and Neermahal lake palace are famous monuments.

question: Who is the author of the book titled 'The White Tiger'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aravind Adiga.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• 'The White Tiger' (2008) is the debut novel of Indian-Australian writer Aravind Adiga; it won the Man Booker Prize in 2008. (मैन बुकर पुरस्कार)

• The novel is written as a series of letters by its narrator Balram Halwai, a village boy who rises to become an entrepreneur in Bengaluru, and satirises India's class divide.

• It was adapted into a Netflix film (2021) directed by Ramin Bahrani, starring Adarsh Gourav, Priyanka Chopra and Rajkummar Rao.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Mulk Raj Anand — 'Untouchable', 'Coolie', 'Two Leaves and a Bud', 'The Village'.

• Ravinder Singh — 'I Too Had a Love Story', 'Can Love Happen Twice?', 'Your Dreams Are Mine Now'.

• Khushwant Singh — 'Train to Pakistan', 'The Company of Women', 'Delhi: A Novel', 'Truth, Love and a Little Malice'.

NOTE

• Other works by Aravind Adiga: 'Between the Assassinations', 'Last Man in Tower', 'Selection Day', 'Amnesty'.

• Indian-origin Booker Prize winners: V.S. Naipaul (1971), Salman Rushdie (1981, Midnight's Children), Arundhati Roy (1997, The God of Small Things), Kiran Desai (2006, The Inheritance of Loss), Aravind Adiga (2008).

question: Which Mughal ruler was overthrown by British and sent to exile in Burma, after the revolt of 1857?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bahadur Shah II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bahadur Shah II (Bahadur Shah Zafar) was the last Mughal Emperor; after the failure of the Revolt of 1857, the British captured him at Humayun's Tomb, tried him and exiled him to Rangoon (Burma/Myanmar) in 1858, where he died in 1862. (अंतिम मुगल सम्राट)

• The rebel sepoys who captured Delhi on 11 May 1857 proclaimed him the symbolic leader/Emperor of Hindustan; his sons were shot dead by Major William Hodson.

• The revolt ended Company rule — by the Government of India Act, 1858 (Queen's Proclamation), the administration passed to the British Crown.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bahadur Shah I (Shah Alam I) — son of Aurangzeb, ruled 1707–1712; his reign began the period of later Mughals.

• Shah Jahan (1628–1658) — builder of the Taj Mahal, Red Fort and Jama Masjid; imprisoned by his son Aurangzeb at Agra Fort.

• Alamgir II (1754–1759) — a weak later Mughal, during whose reign the Third Battle of Panipat (1761) era conflicts and the Battle of Plassey (1757) took place.

NOTE

• Centres and leaders of 1857: Delhi — Bahadur Shah II/General Bakht Khan; Kanpur — Nana Saheb/Tatya Tope; Lucknow — Begum Hazrat Mahal; Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai; Bareilly — Khan Bahadur Khan; Bihar (Jagdishpur) — Kunwar Singh.

• The revolt started at Meerut on 10 May 1857, triggered by the greased cartridges of the Enfield rifle; Mangal Pandey of Barrackpore was hanged on 8 April 1857.

question: Who among the following continues to be hailed as the empress of Bharatanatyam across the world?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tanjore Balasaraswati.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tanjore Balasaraswati (1918–1984), popularly known as Balasaraswati, was the legendary Bharatanatyam dancer who is universally hailed as the "empress of Bharatanatyam". (भरतनाट्यम)

• She was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1957) and the Padma Vibhushan (1977), and belonged to a celebrated family of temple musicians and dancers of Tamil Nadu.

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on the Natya Shastra of Bharata Muni; it was earlier known as Sadir/Dasiattam.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Shovana Narayan — an eminent Kathak exponent (dance of Uttar Pradesh), Padma Shri awardee, disciple of Birju Maharaj.

• Mallika Sarabhai — noted Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dancer-activist, daughter of Vikram Sarabhai and Mrinalini Sarabhai, associated with Darpana Academy, Ahmedabad.

• Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma — known as the "mother of Mohiniyattam", who revived the classical dance of Kerala.

NOTE

• Eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Sattriya (Assam).

• Other Bharatanatyam greats: Rukmini Devi Arundale (founder of Kalakshetra), Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam, Sonal Mansingh.

question: With which country does India share the longest border?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bangladesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India shares its longest land border with Bangladesh, measuring about 4,096.7 km. (सबसे लंबी अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सीमा)

• Five Indian States touch Bangladesh: West Bengal (longest, about 2,217 km), Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

• The India–Bangladesh boundary is based on the Radcliffe Line (1947); the Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) exchanging enclaves was implemented in 2015 through the 100th Constitutional Amendment Act.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• China — about 3,488 km, the second longest, demarcated by the McMahon Line; touches Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.

• Pakistan — about 3,323 km, marked by the Radcliffe Line; touches Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.

• Nepal — about 1,751 km; Myanmar about 1,643 km; Bhutan about 699 km; Afghanistan about 106 km (shortest, through the Durand Line region).

NOTE

• Indian State with the longest international border — Jammu & Kashmir (traditionally counted); among States, West Bengal touches the most (Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan).

• Border-guarding forces: BSF (Pakistan and Bangladesh), ITBP (China), SSB (Nepal and Bhutan), Assam Rifles (Myanmar).

question: Which among the following is a dance performed by the devotees during the ceremonial worship of Murugan the Hindu God of war?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kavadi attam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kavadi attam ("burden dance") is a ceremonial folk dance of Tamil Nadu performed by devotees during the worship of Lord Murugan, the Hindu God of war. (कावड़ी आट्टम)

• Devotees carry a decorated wooden or bamboo arch called the kavadi on their shoulders, dancing to the beat of drums as an act of penance and fulfilment of vows.

• It is closely associated with the festival of Thaipusam, celebrated in the Tamil month of Thai, and with the famous Murugan temple at Palani.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Mayilattom — the peacock dance of Tamil Nadu and Kerala, in which dancers dress as peacocks and perform in Subrahmanya (Murugan) temples.

• Yakshagana — a traditional theatre-dance form of coastal Karnataka combining dance, music, dialogue and elaborate costumes.

• Kummi — a simple folk dance of Tamil Nadu performed in a circle by women who clap their hands rhythmically, usually during Pongal and temple festivals.

NOTE

• Other folk dances of Tamil Nadu: Karagattam, Kolattam, Oyilattam, Devarattam, Puliyattam, Poikkal Kudirai Attam.

• Lord Murugan (Kartikeya/Subrahmanya) has six famous abodes in Tamil Nadu called the Arupadai Veedu — Palani, Swamimalai, Thiruchendur, Thiruthani, Pazhamudircholai and Thirupparamkunram.

question: Cultivation of cotton requires how many frost-free days?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 210.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Cotton requires high temperature, light rainfall or irrigation, 210 frost-free days and bright sunshine for its growth. (कपास — 210 पालारहित दिन)

• It is a kharif crop that grows best in the black soil (regur/black cotton soil) of the Deccan plateau and takes 6 to 8 months to mature.

• India is one of the largest producers of cotton; major producing States are Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telangana, Karnataka, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Cotton is the main raw material of the cotton textile industry, India's largest and oldest organised industry; the first modern cotton mill was set up in Mumbai in 1854.

• Cotton is one of the fibre crops along with jute, hemp and natural silk; jute grows in well-drained fertile alluvial soil in flood plains.

NOTE

• Crop conditions: Rice — above 25°C and above 100 cm rainfall; Wheat — 50 to 75 cm rainfall, cool growing season and bright sunshine at ripening; Tea — warm, moist, frost-free climate with well-drained loamy soil.

• Bt cotton is the genetically modified cotton variety approved in India in 2002; the Technology Mission on Cotton was launched in 2000.

question: Which country hosted the World Championships in Athletics (18th) in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is United States of America.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 18th World Athletics Championships were held from 15 to 24 July 2022 at Hayward Field, Eugene, Oregon in the United States of America. (विश्व एथलेटिक्स चैंपियनशिप)

• This was the first time the World Athletics Championships were hosted on US soil; the USA topped the medal tally with 33 medals (13 gold).

• Neeraj Chopra won the silver medal in the men's javelin throw (88.13 m) — India's first-ever silver and only its second medal at the World Athletics Championships after Anju Bobby George's bronze in 2003.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The 2019 (17th) edition was held in Doha, Qatar; the 2023 (19th) edition was held in Budapest, Hungary, and the 2025 edition in Tokyo, Japan.

• The World Athletics Championships are organised by World Athletics (formerly IAAF), founded in 1912, headquartered in Monaco; President — Sebastian Coe.

NOTE

• Neeraj Chopra won gold at the Tokyo Olympics 2020 (held 2021) and at the World Athletics Championships 2023, Budapest.

• Anju Bobby George won bronze in the long jump at the 2003 Paris World Championships — India's first-ever medal in the event.

question: Which among the following Vitamins plays an essential role in vision?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vitamin A (Retinol) is essential for vision — it forms the visual pigment rhodopsin in the rod cells of the retina, which enables sight in dim light. (विटामिन ए — दृष्टि)

• Its deficiency causes night blindness (nyctalopia), xerophthalmia and dryness of the cornea.

• Sources: carrot, papaya, mango, green leafy vegetables, milk, butter, egg yolk, liver and fish liver oil; it is a fat-soluble vitamin.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid) — deficiency causes scurvy (bleeding gums); found in amla, citrus fruits, guava and tomato.

• Vitamin B1 (Thiamine) — deficiency causes beri-beri; found in whole grains, pulses and nuts.

• Vitamin D (Calciferol) — deficiency causes rickets in children and osteomalacia in adults; synthesised in the skin from sunlight.

NOTE

• Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K; Water-soluble vitamins: B-complex and C.

• Other deficiency diseases: Vitamin B2 — cheilosis; Vitamin B3 — pellagra; Vitamin B12 — pernicious anaemia; Vitamin E — sterility; Vitamin K — delayed blood clotting.

question: Pandit Ravi Shankar was awarded India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 1999. He played which of the following instruments?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sitar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Ravi Shankar (1920–2012) was the world-renowned Indian musician who played the sitar, a plucked string instrument of Hindustani classical music. (सितार)

• He was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1999, along with the Padma Bhushan (1967), Padma Vibhushan (1981) and multiple Grammy Awards.

• He popularised Indian classical music in the West, taught George Harrison of the Beatles, and belonged to the Maihar gharana, being a disciple of Ustad Allauddin Khan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bansuri (flute) — a wind instrument; famous exponents: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, Pannalal Ghosh.

• Tabla — a percussion instrument; famous exponents: Ustad Zakir Hussain, Ustad Alla Rakha, Pandit Kishan Maharaj.

• Shehnai — a wind instrument; Ustad Bismillah Khan, who received the Bharat Ratna in 2001, was its greatest exponent.

NOTE

• Musicians awarded the Bharat Ratna: M.S. Subbulakshmi (1998), Pandit Ravi Shankar (1999), Ustad Bismillah Khan (2001), Bhimsen Joshi (2008), Lata Mangeshkar (2001), Bhupen Hazarika (2019, posthumous).

• Instruments and artists: Sarod — Ustad Amjad Ali Khan; Santoor — Pandit Shivkumar Sharma; Violin — Dr. L. Subramaniam; Veena — S. Balachander; Mridangam — Palghat Mani Iyer.

question: National income received by the households is called ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is personal income.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Personal Income is that part of the national income which is actually received by households (individuals) and non-corporate businesses from all sources before payment of direct taxes. (व्यक्तिगत आय)

• Formula: Personal Income = National Income − Undistributed corporate profits − Corporate taxes − Net interest paid by households + Transfer payments to households from government and firms.

• Personal income differs from national income because a part of income earned is not received (retained profits, corporate tax) and a part received is not earned (transfer payments such as pensions and unemployment allowance).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Disposable (personal) income = Personal Income − Direct/personal taxes — the income actually available with households for consumption and saving.

• Domestic income (NDP at factor cost) is the income generated within the domestic territory of a country, whereas national income adds net factor income from abroad (NFIA).

• There is no standard national-income aggregate called "professional income".

NOTE

• National Income = NNP at factor cost = GNP − Depreciation − Net Indirect Taxes; GNP = GDP + NFIA.

• In India, national income estimates are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation; the first estimate was made by Dadabhai Naoroji ("Poverty and Un-British Rule in India").

question: Which among the following rivers does not flow into the Bay of Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tapti.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Tapti (Tapi) is a west-flowing river that rises at Multai in Betul district, Madhya Pradesh, and drains into the Arabian Sea through the Gulf of Khambhat — not into the Bay of Bengal. (ताप्ती — अरब सागर)

• It flows through Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat, is about 724 km long, and flows in a rift valley parallel to the Narmada, between the Satpura ranges.

• The port city of Surat is situated on the banks of the Tapti; the Ukai (Kakrapar) project is built on it.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Krishna — rises near Mahabaleshwar (Western Ghats, Maharashtra) and falls into the Bay of Bengal; tributaries — Bhima, Tungabhadra, Koyna, Musi.

• Yamuna — the longest tributary of the Ganga, rises from the Yamunotri glacier; the Ganga system finally drains into the Bay of Bengal.

• Mahanadi — rises in Chhattisgarh and drains into the Bay of Bengal in Odisha; the Hirakud Dam (longest earthen dam) is built on it.

NOTE

• West-flowing (Arabian Sea) rivers: Narmada, Tapti, Mahi, Sabarmati, Luni, Periyar, Sharavati; the Narmada and Tapti flow through rift valleys and form estuaries.

• East-flowing (Bay of Bengal) rivers: Ganga, Brahmaputra, Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Subarnarekha, Penner — most of them form deltas.

question: As per the contents mentioned in Asokan inscriptions, how many major political centres were there in the Mauryan empire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is five.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to Asokan inscriptions, the Mauryan empire had five major political centres — the capital Pataliputra and the provincial centres of Taxila, Ujjayini, Tosali and Suvarnagiri. (मौर्य साम्राज्य के पाँच राजनीतिक केंद्र)

• Taxila guarded the north-west, Ujjayini the route to western/central India, Tosali (Kalinga, Odisha) the east, and Suvarnagiri ("golden mountain", Karnataka) the gold-rich south.

• Provinces were governed by princes of royal blood called Kumara/Aryaputra, assisted by officials such as Mahamatras and Rajukas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Mauryan empire was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322/321 BCE with the help of Chanakya (Kautilya), author of the Arthashastra.

• Ashoka (268–232 BCE) fought the Kalinga War in 261 BCE, after which he embraced Buddhism; his inscriptions were first deciphered by James Prinsep in 1837.

• Ashokan edicts are mostly in Prakrit language written in the Brahmi script (Kharosthi in the north-west, Greek and Aramaic at Shahbazgarhi/Kandahar).

NOTE

• Ashoka's inscriptions are classified as Major Rock Edicts (14), Minor Rock Edicts, Major Pillar Edicts (7), Minor Pillar Edicts and Cave inscriptions (Barabar caves).

• The Sarnath Lion Capital of Ashoka was adopted as the National Emblem of India on 26 January 1950; the motto "Satyameva Jayate" is from the Mundaka Upanishad.

question: Who among the following freedom fighters gave the famous quote "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!"?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subhash Chandra Bose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous slogan "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom!" ("तुम मुझे खून दो, मैं तुम्हें आज़ादी दूंगा") was given by Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose in a speech at Burma (Myanmar) in July 1944.

• Bose organised the Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army) and set up the Provisional Government of Free India (Azad Hind Government) at Singapore on 21 October 1943.

• His other famous slogans were "Jai Hind" and "Dilli Chalo"; he founded the Forward Bloc in 1939 after resigning from the Congress presidentship (Tripuri session).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel — the "Iron Man of India", leader of the Bardoli Satyagraha (1928) and the architect of the integration of princely states; first Deputy PM and Home Minister.

• Bal Gangadhar Tilak — "Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it"; called Lokmanya and the "Father of Indian Unrest".

• Lala Lajpat Rai — the "Punjab Kesari", died of injuries from a lathi-charge during the Simon Commission protest in 1928.

NOTE

• Famous slogans: "Do or Die" — Mahatma Gandhi (Quit India, 1942); "Inquilab Zindabad" — Bhagat Singh/Hasrat Mohani; "Vande Mataram" — Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay; "Sare Jahan Se Achha" — Muhammad Iqbal.

• Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose was born on 23 January 1897 at Cuttack, Odisha; his birth anniversary is celebrated as Parakram Diwas.

question: The Fifth Khelo India Youth Games 2022 was organised in ______ in 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 5th Khelo India Youth Games 2022 were held in Madhya Pradesh from 30 January to 11 February 2023, with Bhopal, Indore, Gwalior, Jabalpur, Ujjain, Maheshwar, Khargone and Balaghat as venues. (खेलो इंडिया यूथ गेम्स)

• Maharashtra topped the medal tally (161 medals, 56 gold), followed by Madhya Pradesh (2nd) and Haryana (3rd).

• The mascot was "Mowgli" (from The Jungle Book) and the games were organised by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Previous editions: 1st — New Delhi (2018), 2nd — Pune, Maharashtra (2019), 3rd — Guwahati, Assam (2020), 4th — Panchkula, Haryana (2021, held in 2022).

• The 6th Khelo India Youth Games were held in Tamil Nadu (Chennai) in 2024.

NOTE

• The Khelo India programme was launched in 2018 to revive sports culture and identify talent at the grassroots; it includes the Khelo India Youth Games, Khelo India University Games and Khelo India Winter Games.

• Major sports awards of India: Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (highest), Arjuna Award (outstanding performance), Dronacharya Award (coaches), Dhyan Chand Award (lifetime achievement), Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar.

question: Which among the following famous temples is located in Assam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kamakhya Temple.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Kamakhya Temple is situated on the Nilachal Hill in Guwahati, Assam, on the bank of the Brahmaputra river, and is dedicated to Goddess Kamakhya. (कामाख्या मंदिर, असम)

• It is one of the most important Shakti Peethas, where the yoni (womb) of Goddess Sati is believed to have fallen; it is a major centre of Tantric worship.

• The famous Ambubachi Mela is held here every year in June (Ashadha), attracting lakhs of devotees and tantriks.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Somnath Temple — at Veraval, Gujarat; the first among the twelve Jyotirlingas of Lord Shiva, repeatedly plundered (notably by Mahmud of Ghazni in 1025) and rebuilt, last reconstructed under Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

• Shore Temple — at Mahabalipuram, Tamil Nadu, built by the Pallava ruler Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha); a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• Mundeshwari Temple — in Kaimur district, Bihar, regarded as one of the oldest functional Hindu temples in India.

NOTE

• Other famous sites of Assam: Kaziranga National Park (one-horned rhinoceros), Manas National Park, Majuli (largest river island), Sivasagar (Ahom monuments), Umananda Temple.

• Assam's festivals: Bihu (Rongali/Bohag, Kongali/Kati, Bhogali/Magh); classical dance — Sattriya.

question: When did the Chauri Chaura incident take place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1922.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Chauri Chaura incident took place on 5 February 1922 at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district, Uttar Pradesh, when an angry mob of protesters set fire to a police station, killing 22 policemen. (चौरी चौरा कांड)

• Shocked by the violence, Mahatma Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement on 12 February 1922 (formally ratified by the Congress Working Committee at Bardoli).

• The Non-Cooperation Movement had been launched in 1920 at the Nagpur session, merged with the Khilafat Movement led by the Ali brothers (Maulana Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• 1901 — no major national movement event; 1908 — Bal Gangadhar Tilak was sentenced to six years' transportation to Mandalay.

• 1915 — Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa (9 January 1915, now celebrated as Pravasi Bharatiya Divas); the Ghadar/Home Rule background events also belong to this period.

• After the withdrawal, leaders like C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party in 1923.

NOTE

• Gandhian movements: Champaran Satyagraha (1917), Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918), Kheda Satyagraha (1918), Non-Cooperation (1920–22), Civil Disobedience/Dandi March (1930), Quit India (1942).

• The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred on 13 April 1919 at Amritsar under General Dyer, which led to the launch of the Non-Cooperation Movement.

question: Polyatomic positive ions often have common names ending with the suffix ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is -onium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Polyatomic positive ions (cations) — ions made of more than one atom carrying a positive charge — commonly have names ending with the suffix "-onium". (बहुपरमाणुक धनायन)

• Examples: ammonium (NH₄⁺), hydronium (H₃O⁺), phosphonium (PH₄⁺), sulfonium, oxonium.

• In contrast, most common polyatomic anions end in "-ate" or "-ite" (sulphate SO₄²⁻, sulphite SO₃²⁻, nitrate NO₃⁻, nitrite NO₂⁻).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• -ide is used for monoatomic negative ions — chloride (Cl⁻), oxide (O²⁻), sulphide (S²⁻), nitride (N³⁻); also for a few polyatomic anions such as hydroxide and cyanide.

• -ic and -ous are older (common) suffixes showing the higher and lower oxidation states of a metal — ferric (Fe³⁺) and ferrous (Fe²⁺), cupric (Cu²⁺) and cuprous (Cu⁺).

• "-ic" is also used in naming acids (sulphuric acid from sulphate) and "-ous" for acids of lower oxidation state (sulphurous acid from sulphite).

NOTE

• Common polyatomic ions: NH₄⁺ (ammonium), OH⁻ (hydroxide), NO₃⁻ (nitrate), CO₃²⁻ (carbonate), HCO₃⁻ (bicarbonate), SO₄²⁻ (sulphate), PO₄³⁻ (phosphate), MnO₄⁻ (permanganate), CrO₄²⁻ (chromate).

• A cation is formed by loss of electrons and moves to the cathode; an anion is formed by gain of electrons and moves to the anode during electrolysis.

question: In India, census is conducted under the provisions of the Census Act ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1948.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In India, the census is conducted under the provisions of the Census Act, 1948, which provides the legal framework, the duties of citizens and enumerators, and the confidentiality of individual data. (जनगणना अधिनियम, 1948)

• The census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

• Census is a Union subject under Entry 69 of the Union List in the Seventh Schedule, and is mentioned in Article 246 of the Constitution.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The first complete/synchronous census in India was conducted in 1881 under Lord Ripon; the first (non-synchronous) attempt was made in 1872 under Lord Mayo.

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th after Independence; its slogan was "Our Census, Our Future".

NOTE

• Census 2011 data: Population 121.09 crore; sex ratio 943; literacy rate 74.04%; density 382 persons per sq km; decadal growth 17.7%.

• Most populous State — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim; highest literacy — Kerala; lowest literacy — Bihar; highest sex ratio — Kerala; lowest sex ratio — Haryana.

question: A maximum of ______ members can be nominated by the President of India to become the member of the Rajya Sabha.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The President of India can nominate a maximum of 12 members to the Rajya Sabha from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art and social service. (राज्यसभा में 12 नामित सदस्य)

• This is provided under Article 80 of the Constitution; the Fourth Schedule deals with the allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to States and Union Territories.

• The maximum strength of the Rajya Sabha is 250 (238 representatives of States and UTs + 12 nominated); the present actual strength is 245.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Rajya Sabha members are elected by the elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies through the single transferable vote system of proportional representation.

• The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house (not subject to dissolution); one-third of its members retire every two years, and each member has a term of six years.

• The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Article 64).

NOTE

• Maximum strength of the Lok Sabha is 550 (530 from States + 20 from UTs) under Article 81; the earlier provision for two nominated Anglo-Indian members was discontinued by the 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019.

• Minimum age: 30 years for Rajya Sabha and 25 years for Lok Sabha membership.

question: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Amendment Bill, 2021 seeks to amend Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2015.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Amendment Bill, 2021 seeks to amend the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015. (किशोर न्याय अधिनियम, 2015)

• The 2021 amendment authorises District Magistrates and Additional District Magistrates to issue adoption orders (earlier done by civil courts) and to monitor Child Welfare Committees and District Child Protection Units.

• It also strengthened the eligibility criteria for members of Child Welfare Committees (CWCs) and re-categorised certain serious offences against children.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The JJ Act, 2015 replaced the Juvenile Justice Act, 2000 and allowed children in the age group of 16–18 years to be tried as adults for heinous offences, subject to a preliminary assessment by the Juvenile Justice Board.

• The Act came in the wake of the 2012 Nirbhaya case and is administered by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

• The Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA) is the nodal body for adoption of Indian children.

NOTE

• Constitutional provisions for children: Article 15(3) (special provisions for women and children), Article 21A (free and compulsory education for 6–14 years), Article 24 (prohibition of employment of children below 14 in hazardous work), Article 39(e) and (f).

• Related laws: POCSO Act, 2012, Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016, Right to Education Act, 2009, Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006.
